archetypes.name: parity-map
archetypes.rationale: Plan claims ~40 backing functions as have/partial/gap but those claims may not match what actually exists in the Python modules — silent under-statement of gaps causes implementation surprises.
archetypes.prompt_body: For each row in the domain→verb→backing mapping tables, verify the stated status (have/partial/gap) against the actual contents of the referenced Python module (git.py, push.py, rebase.py, pr.py, gh.py, ci_monitor.py). Specifically check whether every 'have' row names a function that exists with the KV keys and exit codes the plan describes, and whether every 'partial' row correctly characterises the missing contract surface rather than understating a full gap. Flag rows where the plan's status label understates the work required, where the named backing function does not exist under that name, or where the described KV contract differs from what the existing function signature implies. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: deletion-gate
archetypes.rationale: The Deferred-to-E1 transitive closure list is hand-enumerated from ship-pr.sh callees; an incomplete list causes premature deletion of a retained script and breaks the bash ship-pr path.
archetypes.prompt_body: Trace the actual $SCRIPT_DIR/X.sh invocations in scripts/ship-pr.sh and all scripts it sources (implement-finalize.sh, lint-fix-loop.sh, and any further hops) to verify the Deferred-to-E1 list is complete — flag any callee present in the repo but absent from the plan's retention table. Also compare the plan's description of the migration_lint upgrade (match manifest full paths plus $SCRIPT_DIR-derived forms; live-invocation-only ship-pr blocker; no bare-basename substring) against the existing python/migration_lint.py implementation to identify discrepancies between what the plan promises to build and what would actually be needed given the current code. Check whether check-remote-branch.sh's conditional deferral (deletable only after finalize.py is repointed) is consistently reflected across the deletion sequence, the Deferred-to-E1 table, and the files-to-modify section. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
